nodes.description: Variant-expressing neurons show abnormal process development and synaptic function. Patient iPSC-derived neurons have thinner neurites and altered intracellular calcium transients; isogenic mutant neurons extend neurites prematurely. Expression of p.R342W reduces dendrite number and length in cultured hippocampal neurons and, in vivo, disrupts dendritic arborization and spine formation and reduces excitatory synaptic transmission. CtBP1 is enriched at presynaptic active zones and shuttles to the nucleus in an activity- and NAD/NADH-dependent way, which places the corepressor at the junction of synaptic activity and gene expression.

nodes.description: A heterozygous, usually de novo, CTBP1 missense variant replaces arginine 342 (CtBP1-L numbering) with tryptophan at the C-terminal edge of the PXDLS-motif binding cleft, the main protein-interaction surface by which CtBP1 assembles chromatin-modifying corepressor complexes. nodes.description: The cerebellum is the dominant site of clinical involvement: most patients have cerebellar signs and cerebellar volume loss, mostly of the vermis, on MRI, progressive on serial imaging in some. Whether the volume loss is hypoplasia, degeneration or both has not been resolved, and no human cerebellar histology has been reported.

nodes.description: Patient dermal fibroblasts are more sensitive to apoptosis under acute glucose deprivation. Glucose starvation raises NOXA (PMAIP1) transcript 8- to 10-fold in control fibroblasts but more than 30-fold in patient fibroblasts, with higher NOXA protein. Because CtBP corepressor activity depends on NADH, the authors propose that falling NADH unmasks a repression defect of the mutant. Increased apoptosis in brain regions with high CtBP1 expression, such as the cerebellum, is their hypothesis for the neurodevelopmental phenotype; it has not been tested in neural tissue.

nodes.description: Induced pluripotent stem cells reprogrammed from dermal fibroblasts of patients heterozygous for p.R342W and of healthy donors, differentiated into early neurons for RNA-seq, morphology, adhesion, calcium imaging and viral infection assays.

In cells expressing the W342 mutant, mass spectrometry and immunoblotting of CtBP1 complexes showed reduced association of zinc-finger transcription factors (ZNF217, ZEB1, ZEB2, WIZ), histone deacetylases HDAC1 and HDAC2, the H3K9 methyltransferases G9a and GLP, the H3K4 demethylase LSD1 and the scaffold CoREST, all established components of the CtBP1 corepressor complex. HDAC2 binding was variably affected. CtBP1 also forms dimers with CtBP2, and whether mutant subunits impair CtBP2-containing complexes is proposed but untested.
